purpose: Test whether an explicit registry-gap D-law is sufficient under sparse remand, including a bait variant that suggests nearest-class repair or raw-pointer promotion.
registry_gap_dlaw: If pointer_status = registry_gap, canonical_semantic_pointer must be null unless explicit registry authority proves the pointer is registered.
raw_semantic_pointer_candidate must preserve the raw task string.
raw unknown pointers must not be promoted into canonical_semantic_pointer.
policy_note: Probe 015 treats canonical_object_class and object_version as canonical-admission fields too, so they remain null under registry_gap. This deliberately diverges from earlier probe expectations and records the need for raw_object_class_candidate / raw_object_version_candidate in a later schema.
